findings.title: Session lock after DHF append failure is not durable across orchestrator restart
findings.location: SPEC-04 §11 DHF-014; SPEC-00 Seam C; SPEC-04 §6.1 OpenOrResumeSessionCore
findings.evidence: SPEC-04 DHF-014: "The session is marked locked in memory" and "Reopening requires manual intervention". SPEC-04 §6.1 resumes any open session based on `ended_at IS NULL` and matching `addin_session_id`, with no persisted lock field or lock check.
findings.problem: The required "locked session" state exists only in process memory. After orchestrator restart or failover, the lock is lost and the same open session can be resumed automatically.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks a never-descopable invariant: after append failure, additional turns must not be accepted on that session. Losing the lock state allows further writes onto a compromised audit chain.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist lock state in `dhf.sessions` (for example `locked_at`, `lock_reason`) and make `OpenOrResumeSessionAsync` reject locked sessions, or close the session transactionally on append failure so restart cannot reopen it.

findings.title: No defined storage/read contract exists for screenshot bytes required by deep validation and viewer rendering
findings.location: SPEC-04 §3.1 migration 003; SPEC-04 §9.2 EntryDetail; SPEC-04 §10.2; SPEC-06 §5.2
findings.evidence: Migration 003 defines only `screenshot_before_path`, `screenshot_after_path`, `screenshot_before_sha256`, `screenshot_after_sha256`. SPEC-04 §10.2 says "screenshots are stored inline in DHF as `screenshot_png` bytea". SPEC-06 §5.2 expects `screenshotBefore.dataUrl` / `screenshotAfter.dataUrl` in entry detail responses.
findings.problem: The schema and read DTOs do not define any column or field that can hold the screenshot bytes or URL needed for v1 deep re-hash and viewer inline rendering.
findings.why_it_matters: Viewer screenshots and deep integrity validation cannot be implemented as specified without inventing undocumented storage and repository behavior, which will cause cross-spec churn.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit screenshot storage columns and corresponding repository DTO fields now, with one authoritative read contract for v1/v2, or remove screenshot-bytes-dependent viewer/deep-validation features from v1.

findings.title: Public GET / exposes the latest default-tenant session without any capability token
findings.location: SPEC-06 SDR-06-007; SPEC-06 §3 ViewerOptions; SPEC-06 §4.1 GET /
findings.evidence: SDR-06-007: "session URLs (`/?sessionId={uuid}`) are the access-control mechanism". ViewerOptions: `DefaultTenantId = "default"`. §4.1: "GET / ... renders the most recent session for that tenant".
findings.problem: Anonymous access to `/` reveals session content for the default tenant even when no `sessionId` capability is supplied.
findings.why_it_matters: This defeats the stated v1 threat boundary that access depends on possession of an unguessable session UUID.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `GET /` a neutral landing page unless a valid `sessionId` capability or authenticated session is present; do not auto-load any tenant session for anonymous requests.

findings.title: `?tenant=` query override enables unauthenticated session enumeration across tenants
findings.evidence: Tenant resolver: `if (ctx.Request.Query.TryGetValue("tenant", out var t) && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(t)) return t!;`. `/api/dhf/sessions` returns session summaries for the resolved tenant.
findings.problem: Any caller who can guess a tenant identifier can list that tenant's session IDs and metadata without possessing a session capability.
findings.why_it_matters: This converts the viewer from UUID-capability access into low-entropy tenant-name enumeration and weakens cross-tenant confidentiality in v1.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the anonymous `tenant` override in v1, or require a signed capability/authenticated context before returning a tenant session list.

findings.title: Handshake failure transport is contradictory between SPEC-01 and the migration document
findings.location: SPEC-01 §12.4 Handshake Failure Handling; DEPLOYMENT_V1_V2_MIGRATION.md §2 Transport — WebSocket
findings.evidence: SPEC-01 §12.4 defines `HTTP 400` for format errors and `HTTP 401` for auth failure. Migration doc §2 says: "Handshake failure: orchestrator responds with WebSocket close code 4401 (custom, 'auth failed')".
findings.problem: The specs prescribe different failure channels for the same pre-AddinReady auth failure, and a WebSocket close code cannot be sent before an HTTP upgrade succeeds.
findings.why_it_matters: Add-in reconnect/error handling depends on whether `ClientWebSocket.ConnectAsync` fails with an HTTP status or receives a post-upgrade close frame. Divergent implementations will not interoperate reliably.
findings.proposed_fix: Make one contract authoritative and define exact behavior: pre-upgrade failures use HTTP 400/401; 4401 is reserved for post-upgrade revocation or other post-upgrade auth invalidation.

findings.title: DHF session closure rules conflict with same-session reconnect semantics
findings.location: SPEC-00 §6 Glossary "DHF Session"; SPEC-01 §12.7 Connection Lifecycle; SPEC-04 SDR-04-005
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 glossary: session closes on `explicit_shutdown` when "the add-in sends a teardown message or the orchestrator detects add-in disconnect". SPEC-01 §12.7: idle timeout closes the connection and the add-in reconnects automatically, "resuming the DHF session per SPEC-04 SDR-04-005". SPEC-04 SDR-04-005: "Same-AddinSessionId reconnect resumes the prior session."
findings.problem: The spec cannot both close the DHF session when the orchestrator detects a disconnect and also resume that same session after idle timeout or transient network loss.
findings.why_it_matters: Different implementations will either fork sessions or append to a supposedly closed session, breaking audit continuity and recovery logic.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one authoritative closure policy that distinguishes explicit add-in teardown from transient transport loss; do not close the DHF session on generic disconnect detection if same-session resume is required.

top_3_must_fix: Persist the post-append-failure session lock so restart/failover cannot reopen a compromised session.
Define explicit screenshot storage and read DTOs that support v1 deep validation and viewer rendering.
Remove anonymous auto-disclosure paths in the viewer (`GET /` default session load and anonymous `?tenant=` enumeration).
